Dolce&Gabbana Pour Homme (2012) by Dolce&Gabbana is a Aromatic Fougere fragrance for men. Dolce&Gabbana Pour Homme (2012) was launched in 2012. Top notes are Citruses, Bergamot, Neroli and Mandarin Orange; middle notes are Lavender, Sage and Pepper; base notes are Tobacco, Tonka Bean and Cedar.

Designer duo Dolce & Gabbana launched their first perfume Dolce & Gabbana Pour Femme in 1992, followed by its male equivalent Dolce & Gabbana Pour Homme in 1994. Rich floral character of the feminine edition and aromatic - fougere for the masculine one, this perfume pair marked the decade of the nineties. In 2012, the designers have decided to "return to the roots" and to re-launch the two fragrances.

“It’s not so much a reedition as it is a fine-tuning,” said Gabbana to wwd magazine. “We altered the bottles a bit.…There has been an evolution [of the brand] since the Nineties, Domenico and I were much younger then — we’ve really matured a lot.”

Dolce & Gabbana Pour Homme reedition is of aromatic, dry and floral character and opens with notes of tangerine, bergamot and neroli. The heart consists of lavender, sage and pepper and the base includes tobacco, cedar and tonka accords.

The advertising campaign is shot by Mario Testino in Sicily with famous models Laetitia Casta and Noah Mills. The fragrances are available from July 2012 – as 40, 75 and 125 ml Eau de Toilette for men.

In my opinion, Dolce & Gabbana pour Homme is a fresh and transparent scent. It's simple yet complex. One of the great advantages of this perfume is its noticeable evolution over time. Dolce&Gabbana Pour Homme (2012) is the definition of easy elegance—feels right for crisp shirts, weekend coffees, and low-key dinners, the kind of scent that makes being put-together feel effortless. Longevity is a steady 6–8 hours on skin with a clean, gentlemanly sillage that’s noticeable up close and in your trail without ever turning loud. For sure one of the best male fragrance ever made. The vintage version is way better!

justwanttosmellnice 07/28/25 12:26

I like to think that I'm calculated when it comes to fragrance choices, researching every last note to approximate a smell before ever actually smelling it.

Everyone lies to themselves at some point.

D&G Pour Homme was an impulse buy at TJMaxx. I'd read about it on here before, and I knew they switched back to Italian production, so when I read "Made In Italy" I knew it was a decent call. It's a massive 200ml bottle, made in 2020 which I found odd. Turns out that prior to 2023/2024 when D&G changed production, only the 200ml bottles were made in Italy... for some reason.

The scent itself is textbook "pleasant." Starts with a sweet rush of oranges and lemons, really makes the senses work overtime (Any XTC fans here?). What sticks around is a delightful haze of lavender, vanilla, sage, and slightly bitter tobacco. Gets a little spicy at the end, not Bel Ami spicy, but like a pinch of pepper. It's very soft, and quite suave. Extremely versatile too, fresh enough to work with shorts while running errands, but still refined enough to dress up. I have zero experience with the fabled 1994 version (which according to some 20 year old forums, wasn't as incredible as people make it out to be now), nor the French and German ones. The Italian one gives me at least about seven hours with two sprays depending on the season, doesn't fill a room (a good thing in my opinion), and doesn't like the cold. I don't like, nor endorse, overspraying, but if you HAD to do it then I would pick this.

Pour Homme is a very clean version of a lot of scents that're crammed into the "barbershop" genre. Eau Sauvage has that slightly sweaty floral, Guerlain Vetiver is earthy, L'Eau D'Issey (a contemporary of the original D&G Pour Homme) has sour yuzu, and Habit Rouge has that dusty rose. D&G Pour Homme's "dirtiest" aspect is the tobacco, but it lends itself more to a soapiness rather than sweaty skin or a gardener with his pipe.

Some people value bottle design, I'm indifferent vergeing on persnickity (I don't like Le Male's). This is a very simple bottle, its smooth curves reflect the stuff inside. The velveteen box is just... decadent. Real nice. In 200ml form, the design turns downright monolithic, but the large base makes it almost unwieldy. Not that big of a deal, just a note for those it may matter to.

I like Dolce & Gabbana Pour Homme. It's up there with Eau Sauvage for most elegant "summer in a bottle" vibes. Not bad for an unexpected addition to the collection.

Epic Journey Into the Bottled Yonder, 229
-------------------------------------------------------
Purchased August 2024
Part II

ALRIGHT lads. Let me revisit this in text. A beautifully finished product and I shall lay it all out for you like a game of Risk - who will stump the enemy?

This is basically a Mercedes-Benz E Class, and for those who never rode in a Euro car, believe me you will remember the first time. I had that twice in my life. First time was in the '90s with vintage Benzes from the '60s and '70s, and a few from the '90s meaning they were new at the time too. Life changed. Forever remembered. Second time was a 2013 E Class, memorable, including a few aging BMWs, a lovely 2008 3 series and a mind-numbing 2013 4 series in terms of the way it was decked and kitted out from the factory I had never seen a BMW like it.

Those cars will never ever see the light of day, why? They're honest collectibles in a world of throw it out and re-buy it tomorrow. They must be cherished more than driven, unlike the driveable classics from GM, Mopar, and Ford which can be driven as much as cherished.
Once you go through these experiences you can't get your mind off them, and this Dolce & Gabbana Pour Homme reissue 2012 including the 1994 original are among the finest European products of all.

It's almost as if a robot fine tuned this, it knew the balance of ingredients written on paper from ages past. Now it's all computer archived. This fabled robot knew how to keep it honest and usable. I could wear D&GPH probably any time and be happy, even if I "really" don't want it on me and would rather a caged maniac of a motherfucking tiger like Furyo, or One Man Show flankers (whoops I've only mentioned Bogart, but point made).
This bottle has the manly man's blessing, because all real men only need a maximum of three clean/fresh scents in their arsenal of tidal wave and volcanic eruption in a bottle.

This is a must have. If you skipped a shower just wear this instead. Stray cat pissed on your front door, spray this on it. That's how clean it is. It's not synthetic, but even if it is you have a genie in a bottle.

You have one wish, it's to be clean for a while. But don't forget this has a spicy headlining act, and this is the main event! The best part!!! Sting vs. Macho Man Savage. Take off your Swiss and put on a Seiko diver.

Lads this has to be faithful to the '94 original, and I haven't smelt that before. With this though you can smell like the '90s and 2012 at the same time. 'Tis a headturner for classy chicks because this is classy.

Batch: 21O05AC2 from 10th April, 2022.

Type: aromatic citrusy old school cologne (somewhat linear)
Top: citrus with a touch of florals (30 minutes)
Mids: A touch of tobacco. Citrus doesn’t completely disappear (2 hrs)
Base: same but becomes creamier and muskier (6 hours tapers to be skin scent after 3 hrs)
Projection: medium
How much do I like this scent?: 3.5/5
Comments: I compared this to a vintage bottle (the one with the sticker). Although they both have similar DNA, the vintage version is brighter and more present in every way. Even with the age the vintage version is noticeably zestier and has a more natural citrus at the top. The new bottle smells greener and more earthy. The vintage is more natural and has a creamier disposition. Check fresh shows my vintage bottle is from 2024 (batch code 414852, they repeat every 10 years) so it is either from 2004 or 2014. The new bottle is made in France (2022).

M-as-Marin 04/08/25 07:06

It is funny to realize again that instead of chasing the next “big” thing, we can look to the past and find more pleasing scents. This is not the first time this has happened to me this year. I can’t believe I still haven’t reviewed this blast from the past, even though I had a miniature edition in 2017, which, sadly, I don’t remember how it smelled. My answer is a resounding yes for all of you wondering whether this oldie release is still worth buying in 2025 and beyond. However, for those who wish to discover it for the first time, this review is just for you.

TOP NOTES
As the notes suggest, Pour Homme opens up with a fresh burst of citrus. Realistically, you’d be hard-pressed to pinpoint any of the specified citrus notes, but the overall feeling is like a fresh citrus garden. Combined with this zest, soapy Neroli mixes for an invigorating quality that instantly transports me to a sunlit Mediterranean morning.

HEART NOTES
Once the initial citrus fades, the fragrance’s heart takes center stage. I’m a big sucker for lavender-based scents, and this is just what I love in my citrus-oriented perfumes. A hefty dose of lavender that gets more peppery as the fragrance sits longer on your skin.

BASE NOTES
A genius move from D&G was to include a fresh dose of hay-like tobacco into the dry down, creating a warm and inviting finish that lingers on the skin. I’m going to be honest with you: If I hadn’t read the notes online, I wouldn’t have known that the slight sweetness and woodiness were coming from cedar and tonka beans. The overall quality is here, but anyone with years of experience in this hobby will know that the ingredients here were not the most expensive.

OVERALL
I appreciate how Dolce&Gabbana has managed to preserve the classic elements of Pour Homme while still keeping it relevant for today’s modern man. Whether it’s the perfectly crafted bottle, the well-balanced aroma, or the positive comments I receive, Pour Homme remains a standout fragrance in my collection. Not a masterpiece, but not bad at all.

TheDogfatherHTX 09/14/24 01:03

So funny story about this one; I had this fragrance before and I've already reviewed it. My initial thoughts on the fragrance were not too great, so I decided to sell it. After I sold it, I tried it a few more times from a decant I had and I really started to enjoy it. I made the decision to purchase it again just to have it. The thing is, the first bottle I had was made in France, whereas this bottle is made in Italy. Based on my research, the general consensus is that the Italian version is the best, with the French version in second place underneath it. Apparently there's also a UK version that most people don't like. Anyway, I decided I'd do another review to see if and how this one is different from the French version. Let's get into it;

Scent:
The opening is citrusy, fresh spicy, and aromatic. The primary notes I get are citruses, lavender, tobacco, and bergamot. The strongest of the notes are the lavender and citruses. The lavender is your standard designer offering of lavender; aromatic and floral with a bit of spice. The citruses are exactly how they are described; citric and tart. This is followed by the bergamot and tobacco. The bergamot carries the came citric accord but with touches of spice and bitterness, while the tobacco brings its familiar warm and dry accord. The dry down is aromatic, warm, and fresh. The primary notes I get are lavender, tobacco, tonka bean, and cedar. The strongest of the notes are the lavender and tobacco. The lavender takes on more of a spicy licorice accord in the dry down while the tobacco maintains the same warm herbaceous vibe from the opening. This is followed by the tonka bean and cedar. The tonka bean has that signature powdery sweetness that it's known for, while the cedar adds some woodiness in the base. Both the tonka and cedar are very subtle though, and are mostly occluded by the lavender and tobacco.

Performance:
Initial projection is moderate at just outside arms length. Sillage is moderate as well with a noticeable, but not heavy scent trail. After a few hours the projection was right under arms length. The sillage was hanging on with a faint scent trail. At the 8 hour mark the projection and sillage were unchanged. By hour 10 the fragrance was a skin scent. I could still get the odd whiff every once in a while, but there was no scent trail or projection left.

When to wear:
This fragrance has a very versatile DNA and will work in all seasons, day or night, and for any occasion. Office, date night, gym, it can do it all. I feel like this fragrance would really shine in formal occasions, as it just has an air of classiness about it.

Blind buy:
If you enjoy "barbershoppy" fragrances, or just enjoy aromatic fougere fragrances in general, this is a safe blind buy for you.

Final verdict:
So the big question; is this one different from the French version? The answer is undoubtedly yes. When it comes to the scent profile, both the Italian and French versions have a heavy focus on citrus in the opening, lavender throughout, and tonka bean/cedar in the dry down. The biggest and most noticeable difference is with the tobacco note. In the Italian version the tobacco is a primary note throughout the life of the fragrance. In the French version the tobacco is completely absent. I personally really enjoy tobacco notes, so the scent profile of the Italian version is more enjoyable to me. When it comes to performance, the Italian version also comes out on top. Whereas the French version became a skin scent after about 6 hours, the Italian version lasted about 10. Having given both versions a fair trial, I would agree with the general consensus; the Italian version is better. Insist on the Italian, but don't feel bad if you can only find the French as it's still a fine fragrance. Either one will make you smell great in a classic, masculine way.

jcarn90 08/07/24 12:40

As a child of the early 90s, this fragrance is bottled nostalgia...

A few years ago, an old customer of mine and I were discussing fragrances and Pour Homme came up. I expressed to him that the original bottle "with the sticker" is hard to find nowadays. He casually said "I have one at home I never wear, I'll bring it in for you." My jaw dropped and a few hours later I had a vintage bottle in my hands - made in Italy. I loved it, but after a few wears I began to notice some sour top notes and I ended up giving it away to a close friend who was lusting over it.

Flash forward to last week, when out of nowhere, thoughts of it came flooding into my head. I'm not entirely sure why, but I suddenly had a longing for it. After some research, I gathered that the "best" reformulation was supposedly the made in France edition distributed by Shiseido. And while I know nothing can compare to the original, I had to quell my curiosity and buy a bottle, especially at the meager price of $40 USD.

I received my bottle today and I'm wearing it as I type this. I have to say, it's beautiful. This version is well blended and totally worth it's humble price tag. Is it an incredibly dynamic, revolutionary scent? Not particularly. But not everything needs to be an exercise in newness. I find things that echo a history - a capsule, a time when people were different and things were simpler - to be endearing and enjoyable. That being said, I still believe the scent is wonderful and imminently wearable in the 2020s. More so than many new cotton-candy designers and avant-garde niche fragrances. Longevity has been decent at 4-5 hours in and projection is about average.

Concerning the scent itself: this lays somewhere between Versace's the Dreamer and YSL's L'Homme. The scent profile is closer to the Dreamer, with it's combination of "fresh" tobacco and lavender on a tonka-coumarin base, though I find Pour Homme to be much cleaner and rounder than The Dreamer. There's no loudness here. This is intimate. And while it smells almost nothing like YSL's L'homme, there is a certain spiritual connection between the two that makes me smile. It could be the aromachemicals that they share, being from around the same era. I like to think it's the bottled zeitgest of the late 20th century.

Absolutely worth it's humble price, if not for anything but to smell history.

TheDogfatherHTX 12/06/23 22:59

The classic men's Dolce and Gabbana fragrance. I had heard some say this is a 10/10 men's fragrance, so I blind bought it to test it out. Let's discuss;

Scent:
Opening is citrusy, spicy, and aromatic. The main notes I get are citruses, lavendar, sage, and pepper. The strongest of these notes are the citrus and lavender giving it a clean and aromatic feeling, followed by the sage and pepper adding to the aromatics and providing spiciness in the background. The dry down is aromatic, woody, and sweet. The main notes I get are lavender, sage, cedar, and tonka bean. The strongest of these notes are the sage and lavender for a soft and clean aromatic feeling, followed by the cedar and tonka bean for a woody and sweet background. Strangely, I don't get any tobacco at all. I get the feeling the note breakdown may have been changed in the new formulations.

Performance:
Initial projection is strong around 6 feet. Sillage is strong as well with an easily noticeable scent trail. At the three hour mark the projection was about arms length and there was still a moderately noticeable scent trail. Around the 6 hour mark the projection and sillage were wearing off.

When to wear:
This is an all-season day or night time fragrance. It has the versatility to work for any occasion. This is a great pick for the office, but would work for a date as well.

Blind buy:
If you like old-school aromatic fougere fragrances, this is a safe blind buy for you.

Final verdict:
Admittedly, the first time I tried this I wasn't a fan. I even went as far as to put it up for sale on Mercari. But after wearing it again to write the review, it's really grown on me and I quite enjoy it now. Not only that, but everyone else that smelled it on me said it was one of their favorites so far. The performance isn't mind-blowing, but it's on par with other designer fougere fragrances. The bottom line is it smells great, performs respectably, gets compliments, and does all this for around $30-40. That's a winner in my book.

Scent: 8/10
Longevity: 6/10
Sillage: 7/10

Marcosamuel 09/23/23 11:57

Dolce&Gabbana Pour Homme

Es un colonia deliciosa la cual percibo con una sensación medio floral en un inicio, con sus toques de picante (pimienta) y cítrico (bergamota) que se combinan en equilibrio perfecto con el tabaco (profundidad y seriedad) y el haba tonka (dulzor) terminan por desarrollar el carácter definitivo y regalar ante la primera impresión a una persona elegante, fresca y sexy.

Su personalidad es potente, pero amable; dulce, pero fresca, de sensación de redondes. La proyección que transmite es de alguien seguro e interesante, lo cual a los hombres nos encanta mostrar. Su duración me encanta, pudiendo acompañar hasta 6 horas seguido y después el aroma persiste pero a través del contacto más íntimo.

Personalmente me fascina usarla en primavera, en especial para el trabajo o reuniones donde uso ropa formal o sport elegante.

Es una fragancia que percibo tanto para el día como para tarde, aunque me guste más en mañanas frescas o con sol de primavera.

A diferencia de otras fragancias ésta le gusta más a mujeres que a hombres, quienes son las que más me han preguntado por ella.

Pd: en relación de rango de edad para uso, es un aroma que percibo como más preciso para jóvenes adultos o adultos (25 a 50), quienes sabrán explotar todo, todo su potencial.

100% recomendable y de colección

Pd: es una fragancia que pareciera que comparte algo de adn con The Dreamer (EDT) de Versace.

dann.martin 07/28/23 23:23

This was my only perfume for a good ten years of my life.
I remember when, back in 2012, I went to a local store to choose a “real” fragrance, and ended up settling on this one – then recently released. It seemed to me an apropriate fragrance for a young man in his mid-twenties who was about to graduate from Law school.
Almost ten years later, when my third bottle was finished, I decided it was time for something new. And it was this search for a new fragrance the kickstarted my deep dive into the world of perfumes.
Now, a couple of years after, and many dozens of perfumes later, I came across a sample of this old friend.
And.... to my surprise, D&G Pour Homme felt just as fresh, elegant, and challenging this time as it did when I first tried it.
It is so well blended. It feels “fresh” and “warm” at the same time. “Light” but yet “full of presence”. “Mature” and “jovial”. So many contradictions reconciled (hence the “challenging”).
It is extremely versatile in terms of time of year and occasion (it’s casual, it’s smart, it’s formal.... Wear it with jeans or a tuxedo, it doesn't matter).
Someone labeled it “an attempt to bottle the essence of an Italian lover”.
I unfortunately don’t know how the original from 1994 smelled like, so sadly I can’t make any comparison.
This should be a staple in a man's wardrobe.
And in the end, I'm buying another bottle.

I wore the 2012 version in 2013 through 2016 and I thought it was great. Then I got the 200ML Made in France version in 2020.
Both are wonderful, fantastic office scents: light citrus, neroli, lavender, fresh soap, sage, and slight pepper in the background. Not much leather to me, but maybe a little (which is perfect... I don't like overbearing leather notes).
Very easy to wear and easy to like. Hard to offend anyone with this. It won't knock anyone's socks off with the scent, but it's a nice, well-mannered gentlemanly frag with a bit of southern European nostalgia... very nice, and I'll always have a bottle of this, even if they reformulate it again. It fits me: I'm often around people who are very sensitive to fragrance, so I'm not likely to wear Amouage or something choking like that. Yes, DGPH is fairly familiar smell and some say it's common... that's because it's so successful. It's successful because LOTS of people like it. When lots of people like it, the brand will continue to produce it. This is a true 90's holdover (like Acqua Di Gio), but in my mind it's a classic, even though the scent doesn't last as long as some would like.
The price is pretty good per ML, and it's hard to overspray. A universal fragrance for a gentleman, very classy without being obnoxious.

sharpnickelz 09/21/18 05:39

I have no experience with any batch of D&G Pour Homme before 2012.

Although other reviewers mention the citruses and tobacco as being the major players, oddly enough, this comes off more floral to my nose. The lavender and neroli are the stars of the show. I barely get any pepper, and while the citrus is definitely there, all of that subsides quickly.

What you are left with is a gorgeous soapy floral fragrance. I could compare it to other neroli based fragrances like Neroli Portofino Forte or even Dunhill Icon, but it takes a different turn. Rather than being bright and tangy, this is far more soft and creamy, like a luxury bar of soap.

I am a big fan of these types of fragrances, especially for the office or casual wear. However, I do have other soapy frags that are superior, like Mugler Cologne, Prada Infusion Domme, and Prada Amber Pour Homme. What this has going for it though is the floral element, which has this air of innocence and calm, unlike so many other fresh soapy frags, which tend to either be zesty or sporty.

The sillage and longevity are nothing to write home about. It gets close to the skin after about the hour mark and lasts 3-4 hours after that. However, if you spray it on clothing, it lasts quite a bit longer and has a fresh out of the dryer quality.

I give it a solid 7.5/10. Well worth having as part of your collection if you like smelling fresh and clean.

Ryanmmas26 08/21/21 10:24

One of my new faves !!! (Reviewing the Made in France version)

Smell on this is very familiar but at the same time unique (especially with the new wave of ambroxin scents)

This opens up very fresh with some light citrus,but also very aromatic with the lavender and some very light pepper giving this some personality ! The heart of this is my favorite as the scent starts to become more rich as the tobacco comes in and the floral notes creep in giving this additional freshness. The dry down is also amazing though as the tobacco becomes the main player alongside the tonka and cedar making this smell very refined,fresh and rich !!! Other adjectives I’d use to describe this scent are smooth,alluring, and professional smelling

I’ve received quite a few compliments with this and despite being an older scent I’d still say it’s relevant and appealing to this day !!

Performance on this is great as it lasts 8-12 hours with good projection for an hour and a nice silage trail for the duration of the scent life

Overall rating -8.5 out of 10 ! A timeless classic but not a scent I’d say is in my top 5 faves (although very close)

The original D&G Pour Homme was a masterpiece, something that turned heads and drew compliments to anyone who was wearing it. It had a magnetic field that drew anyone within a 5 foot radius towards you. I bought my first bottle of D&G Pour Homme in the summer of 2004 because a male flight attendant was wearing it and it filled the cabin of the plane like a glorious plume of olfactory awesomeness. It made me feel like I was standing in a giant cigar humidifier with the finest spices piled up in it as well. As soon as I got off the plane it was my mission to buy it, and it was seriously the best cologne that I had ever purchased. I was 17 at the time and I was unaware of the sexual power the original D&G PH possessed, but let's just say that was the same year I first experienced a woman, and I accredit 60% of that to D&G. Now, as for the reformulation, it's not the same. It's a lackluster version of what the original pour homme used to be. I can best compare it to an old best friend that you haven't seen in years, but then you randomly run into them. After conversing for a while, and talking about the good times you used to have together you realize that they've changed, you don't know exactly how, but the spark of companionship the two of you used to share is no longer there. The D&G pour homme reformulation is a forgery of a formerly great work of art.
